SALT LAKE CITY, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Co-Diagnostics, Inc. (Nasdaq: CODX) ("Co-Diagnostics" or "the Company"), a molecular diagnostics company with a unique, patented platform for the development of molecular diagnostic tests, today announced that it has filed Articles of Amendment to its Articles of Incorporation (the "Amendment") to effect a reverse stock split of its issued and outstanding common stock at a ratio of 1-for-25 shares (the "Reverse Stock Split"). The Reverse Stock Split will become effective at 12:01 a.m. ET on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The Company's common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "CODX" and will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opens on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The Reverse Stock Split is intended to enable the Company to maintain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market, and to maintain sufficient authorized shares available for issuance to allow the Company to conduct equity financings as needed. The new CUSIP number for the Company's common stock following the Reverse Stock Split will be 189763 303.

At the Special Meeting of Stockholders held on November 13, 2026 (the "Special Meeting"), the Company's stockholders approved an amendment to the Company's Articles of Incorporation, as amended, to effect one or more reverse stock splits of the Company's issued and outstanding shares of common stock, on one or more occasions, at a ratio of not less than 1-for-2, with the cumulative effect of all such reverse stock splits not to exceed 1-for-750, such final ratio or ratios and the timing and number of any reverse stock splits to be determined by the Company's board of directors at any time within twelve months following the Special Meeting, without further approval or authorization of the stockholders. Additional information regarding the Reverse Stock Split approved by stockholders can be found in the Company's definitive proxy statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on October 26, 2026.

The Amendment provides that at the effective time of the Reverse Stock Split, each 25 shares of the Company's issued and outstanding common stock will be automatically combined into one (1) validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable share of common stock, without effecting a change to the par value per share. The Reverse Stock Split will impact all shares of the Company's common stock outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the Reverse Stock Split, as well as the number of shares of common stock available for issuance under the Company's equity incentive plans. In addition, the Reverse Stock Split will effect a reduction in the number of shares of common stock issuable upon the exercise of stock options and warrants outstanding immediately prior to the effectiveness of the Reverse Stock Split with a corresponding increase in the applicable exercise price per share, in each case in accordance with the terms thereof. The Reverse Stock Split will not change the number of shares of capital stock authorized for issuance under our Articles of Incorporation. Based on the 13,044,465 shares of common stock currently outstanding, we expect approximately 521,779 shares of common stock to be issued and outstanding following the Reverse Stock Split.

No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Reverse Stock Split. Stockholders who would otherwise be entitled to receive fractional shares as a result of the Reverse Stock Split will have those shares rounded up to the next whole share. Stockholders with shares in brokerage accounts should direct any questions concerning the reverse stock split to their broker; all other stockholders may direct questions to the Company's transfer agent, VStock Transfer, LLC.

About Co-Diagnostics, Inc.:

Co-Diagnostics, Inc., a Utah corporation, is a molecular diagnostics company that develops, manufactures and markets state-of-the-art diagnostics technologies. The Company's technologies are utilized for tests that are designed using the detection and/or analysis of nucleic acid molecules (DNA or RNA). The Company also uses its proprietary technology to design specific tests for its Co-Dx PCR at-home and point-of-care platform (subject to regulatory review and not currently for sale) and to identify genetic markers for use in applications other than infectious disease.

Melville, New York--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - As previously disclosed, on December 23, 2025, FONAR Corporation (NASDAQ: FONR) ("FONAR" or the "Company") entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Merger Agreement") with FONAR, LLC ("Parent") and Fonar Acquisition Sub, Inc. ("Merger Sub"), pursuant to which, subject to the satisfaction of the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, Parent would acquire the Company in an all-cash merger (the "Merger"). Under Section 3.22(a) of the Merger Agreement, the Merger was conditioned on (a) the affirmative vote of shares representing a majority of the stock outstanding and entitled to vote, voting together as a single class, after giving effect to the respective voting powers of each class of stock, and (b) the affirmative vote of a majority of the votes cast by disinterested stockholders, voting together as a single class after giving effect to the respective voting powers of each class of stock.

On February 2, 2026, plaintiff Bruce Taylor ("Plaintiff"), a purported stockholder of the Company, filed a Verified Stockholder Class Action Complaint (the "Complaint"), on behalf of himself and all other similarly situated stockholders of the Company, in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (the "Court"), captioned Taylor v. Fonar Corporation, et al., C.A. No. 2026-0142-JTL (the "Action"). The Complaint named as defendants the Company, Parent, Merger Sub, and Timothy Damadian, Luciano Bonanni, Robert M. Carrino, Ronald G. Lehman, and Richard E. Turk (the "Individual Defendants" and, together with the Company, Parent, and Merger Sub, the "Defendants").

The Complaint alleged that, under Section 203 of the Delaware General Corporation Law ("Section 203"), the Merger must be conditioned on the affirmative vote of at least 66⅔% of the outstanding voting stock of the Company which is not owned by an interested stockholder, as provided in Section 203(a)(3) (the "Section 203 Vote"). The Complaint further alleged that the Individual Defendants breached their fiduciary duties in connection with the foregoing.

Defendants have denied, and continue to deny, that they committed any violation of law or engaged in any of the wrongful acts that were or could have been alleged in the Action, and expressly maintain that they complied with their fiduciary and other legal duties.

On May 29, 2026, the Company filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") a Current Report on Form 8-K calculating the Section 203 Vote, and the Company received approval of the requisite 66⅔% of the outstanding voting stock of the Company which is not owned by an interested stockholder under Section 203(a)(3) (the "Section 203 Approval").

On June 5, 2026, the Court granted and approved a stipulation and order voluntarily dismissing the Action as moot (the "Dismissal Order"). The Dismissal Order dismissed all claims in the Action with prejudice only as to Plaintiff and without prejudice as to any actual or potential claims of any other members of the putative class, and the Court retained jurisdiction to determine Plaintiff's application for an award of attorneys' fees and expenses (the "Fee and Expense Application"). The Dismissal Order was without prejudice to Plaintiff's ability to subsequently file claims challenging the fairness of the Merger and/or the adequacy of the Company's disclosures in connection with the Merger on any basis other than the adequacy of the Company's disclosures regarding Section 203, and Defendants reserved all rights with respect to any such claims.

Following arm's-length negotiations, the parties to the Action agreed to fully resolve the Fee and Expense Application through a payment to Plaintiff's counsel, which the Company will make and/or cause to be made on behalf of all Defendants, in the amount of $1,600,000 (the "Mootness Fee"). The Company, while denying any and all liability, agreed to the Mootness Fee in the exercise of its business judgment in order to avoid the cost, distraction, and uncertainty of further litigation regarding the Fee and Expense Application. The Court has not been asked to review and will not pass judgment on the payment of the Mootness Fee.

On November 15, 2026, the Court entered a Stipulation and Order Governing Plaintiff's Counsel's Award of Attorneys' Fees and Expenses, Notice of Mootness Fee and Closing the Action (the "Fee Order"). Pursuant to the Fee Order, within thirty (30) calendar days of the later of (i) the Court's entry of the Fee Order or (ii) the provision by Plaintiff's counsel of a Form W-9 and wiring instructions to the Company, the Company will pay or cause to be paid the Mootness Fee to Plaintiff's counsel in full and complete satisfaction of the Fee and Expense Application in connection with the Action. Upon receipt of such payment, Plaintiff and Plaintiff's counsel will be deemed to have fully and completely released all Defendants, and each of their respective subsidiaries, affiliates, parents, divisions, directors, officers, employees, predecessors and successors, managers, equity holders, beneficiaries, members, any related persons or entities, insurers, trustees, administrators, representatives and fiduciaries, successors, assigns and agents, from all claims for attorneys' fees and expenses in connection with the Action.

This Notice is being disseminated pursuant to the Fee Order and constitutes notice to the Company's stockholders, including the members of the putative class, to the extent required under Court of Chancery Rule 23. Pursuant to the Fee Order, within five (5) business days of the dissemination of this notice, the Company will file an affidavit with the Court confirming its compliance with the Fee Order's notice requirement, upon which the Register in Chancery is directed to close the Action on the docket for all purposes.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Tenet Fintech Group Inc. (CSE: PKK) (OTCQB: PKKFF) (FSE: P0T) ("Tenet" or the "Company"), an innovative analytics service provider, owner and operator of the Cubeler Business Hub, today announced its financial results and operating highlights for the three-month and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. Tenet reported revenue of $66,070,573 for the quarter, compared to $192,769 in the third quarter of 2025, and a net profit of $1,593,915 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss of $3,594,470 in the third quarter of 2025. All amounts in this news release are in Canadian dollars unless otherwise indicated.

Q3-2026 Key Financial Figures

  • Total Revenue of $66.07 million

  • Net Profit of $1.59 million

Q3-2026 Operating Highlights

The Company's value-added services to China's real estate development and construction sector supply chains through its GoldRiver and Cubeler Business Hub platforms continued to drive revenue in the third quarter of 2026 and provided a solid foundation to build on. Tenet's November 2025 breakthrough framework agreement with Chengdu Honglongyi Trading Ltd. ("CHTL") was the catalyst for much of the activity on the Company's platforms through the first three quarters of 2026. For most of the first half of 2026, CHTL was the sole customer driving meaningful supply-chain-related activity on the Company's platforms. To reduce its dependency on a single customer, the Company made increasing the number of its supply-chain customers a priority. The Company added five new customers between the latter part of the second quarter and the end of the third quarter, bringing the number of customers that contributed to its supply-chain-related revenue during the third quarter to a total of six, including CHTL.

Tenet officially ceased its operations in China's small-business commercial-lending space by selling its 51% ownership stake in its Asia Synergy Financial Capital ("ASFC") subsidiary during the third quarter of 2026. The transaction aligns with the Company's stated desire to focus its operations in China on data aggregation and supply-chain-related activities. The sale of ASFC not only frees up valuable resources but is expected to provide significant capital that can be allocated to bolster the Company's supply-chain-related activities and data-related service offerings in both China and North America.

Although the Company was still not at the commercialization phase during the third quarter of 2026 when it comes to its data-derived product offering, the Company believes that relevant progress was made toward achieving that objective. Tenet made several enhancements to the Cubeler Business Hub, including the addition of a grant-matching feature for registered members, to make the platform more enticing for SMEs. The Company also enhanced its offering to accountants and bookkeepers with the launch of its BKeeper platform allowing them to offer their SME clients with a host of AI-powered value-added services. Those initiatives, combined with the arrival of a new sales manager, contributed to a noticeable increase in the rate of SME registrations on the Cubeler Business Hub during the quarter. With the increase in the amount of SME data at its disposal during the quarter, the Company was optimistic that the launch of a commercially viable series of Canadian economic indexes could be achieved in relatively short order.

Q3-2026 Financial Results Summary

The Company's reported net income in Q3 was significantly impacted by certain nonrecurring events during the quarter. Those events include: 1) the profit realized on the sale of the Company's ASFC financial services subsidiary; 2) the commission paid related to the $225M minimum guaranteed annual revenue agreement signed with Sum Hung Hang Tai Trading Ltd.; 3) the grant of stock options to directors, officers, employees and consultants; 4) an increase in expected credit loss provision related to prepayments made to certain subcontractors dating back to 2022; and 5) the impairment of intangible assets related to ASFC. Together, these five events accounted for net expenses of a little more than $1.7M for the Company in the third quarter, which explains the lower net income reported for the quarter compared to the previous quarter, despite the quarter-over-quarter revenue increase from Q2-2026 to Q3-2026.

In summary, the Company generated revenue of $66,070,573 for the three-month period and $129,443,140 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to $192,769 for the three-month period and $736,677 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2025.

Total expenses before taxes for the quarter amounted to $63,406,975 compared to $3,702,406 for the same period in 2025. The Company realized a net profit of $1,593,915 for the three-month period and $4,984,526 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $3,594,470 for the three-month period and a net loss of $9,156,663 for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2025.

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- For customers, electric reliability is measured in everyday moments: whether the lights come on in the morning, a business can keep its doors open and power is restored quickly when an outage occurs. For the 21st consecutive year, San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E), a subsidiary of Sempra (NYSE: SRE), has been recognized as the most reliable electric utility in the West. PA Consulting presented SDG&E with the 2026 ReliabilityOne® Award for Outstanding Reliability Performance in the Western region.

Over the past decade, the average SDG&E customer has experienced fewer than one sustained outage a year, while the average amount of time without power from unplanned outages has remained at approximately 70 minutes annually. Momentary interruptions have declined 18% since 2016. In 2025, outage frequency and duration, excluding major event days, were at their lowest levels since 2017.

The results reflect long-term investment in a modern grid, predictive tools that help identify problems earlier and smart-grid technology that can isolate an issue and limit the number of customers affected.

"As we work to improve affordability and deliver energy at the lowest cost possible, safety and reliability will always remain the focus at SDG&E," said Scott Crider, president of SDG&E. "Our customers depend on us to ensure power is there when it's needed most. I'm proud of our employees who work every day to deliver on this commitment and have helped make SDG&E the most reliable utility in the West for 21 years."

Delivering reliable energy around the clock takes more than technology. It takes a skilled local workforce, a resilient supply chain and trusted contractor partnerships. SDG&E's crews live and work in the communities they serve, and they're on call around the clock to maintain the system and restore power quickly. Suppliers and contractors back them up by delivering critical materials when they're needed. Together, they help prevent outages, respond when problems occur and restore power as safely and quickly as possible.

Delivering Reliability More Affordably 
SDG&E also considers cost and efficiency when making the investments that support reliable service. The same technology behind 21 years of top reliability performance, from smart switches that limit outages to AI that helps spot risks sooner, can help the company operate more efficiently and address potential problems before they become larger, more costly repairs.

What 21 Years of Reliability Means for Customers
SDG&E's reliability record rests on investments in people, infrastructure and technology designed to identify risks earlier, limit outages and restore power faster for the 3.6 million people it serves.

  • Seeing Risk Sooner: SDG&E launched Edge Alert Sentinel (EAS), an edge AI collaboration with Qualcomm Technologies and UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography. EAS builds on a network of high-definition cameras and artificial intelligence to support early fire detection. It also works alongside advanced sectionalizing devices that automatically isolate problems on the grid. For customers, that means risks are spotted earlier and fewer homes lose power.
  • A Stronger Grid and Faster Restoration: SDG&E replaced older underground cables and overhead lines, added smart switches that help limit outages, and improved restoration processes to restore power faster. Modernized data systems help teams make quicker decisions and learn from every outage. For customers, that means fewer interruptions, shorter outages, real-time outage updates and an easy-to-use online outage tracking tool.
  • A Culture of Safety: SDG&E was California's first utility to earn Cal/OSHA's elite Voluntary Protection Program safety certification for one of its facilities, exceeding industry standards for operational excellence. For customers, that means a well-trained workforce that keeps safety first while keeping the energy system running.

Independent Oversight, Local Accountability
SDG&E's investments are reviewed by the California Public Utilities Commission through an independent, public process. That oversight helps make sure the work that keeps San Diego's grid among the most reliable in the nation is focused, disciplined and transparent.

"Utilities such as SDG&E are committed to delivering reliable service, enhancing resiliency, and maintaining affordability for their customers," said PA's ReliabilityOne® Program Director Patrick Graves. "Increasingly, technology is being used to augment existing capabilities and improve overall system efficiency. These advancements include more accurate estimated restoration times, the implementation of advanced control systems that allow operators to manage infrastructure through a single user interface, and the integration of hardware and software to streamline restoration efforts. At the same time, utilities are continuing to refine and leverage technology to keep rates affordable and accessible for all customers. At PA, we're proud to be working with utilities that are embracing this kind of innovation to meet evolving customer expectations."

The recognition comes as northern Illinois faces new pressures on its power grid. Families and businesses are using more electricity than ever as homes, vehicles and buildings go electric, and severe storms are becoming more frequent and intense. Since ComEd began its smart grid investments in 2012, those upgrades have helped customers avoid nearly 27 million power interruptions and more than $5 billion in outage-related costs. Overall reliability, measured by how long customers are without power, has improved by more than 75 percent compared with the 2007–2011 average. Drilling of Kari, our first new target, was completed in August. Kari was prioritised due to its all-season access and BoT anomalism from a historic survey. The initial program of 1,275 m was drilled in five holes along an E-W profile, located 2.5 km south of known mineralisation at Aarnivalkea West. Although drilling returned evidence of disseminated sulphide mineralisation within the more deformed host lithologies in three out of five drillholes, no significant gold mineralisation was assayed. The work highlighted the unreliability of historic BoT datasets, justifying Valkea's emphasis on generating a critical mass of new more reliable BoT geochemical data to support targeting on the recommencement of diamond drilling in early January 2027.

Metallurgical test work results for Aarnivalkea West

Exploratory metallurgical test work undertaken by Alfred H Knight (UK) on a ~60 kg composite sample from Aarnivalkea West, with an assayed grade of around 1.0 g/t Au, showed mineralisation to be non-refractory in nature. Whole ore leach testing produced high extractions between 93.5% to 96% (95% at a grind size of 106 microns). In addition, batch flotation test work completed for rougher grind sizes, between 75-150 microns, also yielded high recoveries between ~93 and 96%. The test material has Bond Ball Mill Index of 10.8 kWh/t, classifying it as soft to medium hardness.

About Valkea

Valkea Resources is a geoscience-led exploration company focused on making new gold and base metal discoveries in Northern Finland's Central Lapland Greenstone Belt. Its 350 km2 land package includes six principal project areas that span highly prospective regional geological structures. The Company's leadership and technical team include key contributors to the multi-million-ounce Ikkari gold discovery, made in 2020. Work is underway to make a new discovery using the same systematic and disciplined approach to identifying mineral targets with the best potential for the possibility of becoming mines of the future.

New Ships, Expanded Destinations and Enhanced Guest Experiences Shape Carnival's Next Chapter

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Carnival Cruise Line President Christine Duffy today announced plans for two new ships that will introduce a new class to the Carnival fleet. To be built by long-time partner Fincantieri and delivered in 2033 and 2035, the approximately 130,000-gross-ton LNG-powered ships are intentionally designed on a smaller scale, enabling access to more ports and expanding destination and itinerary choices.

"With a 29-ship fleet, we know our guests appreciate choices," said Duffy. "They love the incredible experiences and amenities on our Excel Class ships, the largest in our fleet, but they also love the intimacy our smaller ships offer. This new class gives us the best of both worlds, helping future-proof our fleet with the flexibility to take America's Cruise Line to even more places in the years ahead."

Duffy also shared a first look at Carnival Destiny, major expansions at Celebration Key, Grand Bahama, enhancements at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay and plans to extend popular onboard benefits ashore. With more than 6.5 million guests sailing each year, Carnival has a unique perspective on what guests want from their vacations and is putting that feedback at the center of what comes next.

"Guests are seeking more choice, more flexibility and more ways to make the most of their time together," said Duffy. "What we are announcing today reflects how we're making Carnival cruise vacations even more personal, connected and fun."

Carnival Destiny Delivers More Choice with More Sea to See

Carnival Destiny, debuting in 2029 and the first of three Ace Class ships, is designed to give guests more ways to shape their cruise vacation around what they enjoy most. Built around its promise of More Sea to See, the ship will bring guests closer to the ocean with more outdoor space, expansive views and venues that make the sea part of the experience. Highlights include:

  • More outdoor pools than any other Carnival ship, including the first outward-facing main pool zone. Throughout the ship there will be eight pools, including six infinity pools, totaling more than 11,200 square feet of water surface,

  • An expansive ocean-front lanai that features several pools and brings dining and bar venues closer to the sea,

  • New premium venues with sweeping multideck ocean views, including a new exclusive pool on Deck 18 Aft, a total of 25 new dining and bar experiences, as well as a reimagined Limelight Lounge.

Carnival Destiny will dedicate nearly twice the space to family venues and attractions compared with Carnival's newest ships, bringing a family zone with mini golf, arcades, dining and other family favorites together in one area. It will also introduce Dr. Seuss Splash Station, a new splash pad inspired by The Cat in the Hat and Thing One and Thing Two, featuring water cannons and a dedicated area for children in swim diapers. The new attraction builds on Carnival's 13-year partnership with Dr. Seuss Enterprises and expands its popular Seuss at Sea programming.

Adults will have more choices of their own, with Carnival Destiny introducing Carnival's first adult-only zone spanning four decks. The zone will feature Carnival's first adult-only staterooms, an expanded Serenity adult-only retreat and an exclusive rooftop pool deck.

More Choice Ashore: The Next Evolution of Paradise Collection

Duffy also shared that Carnival is expanding the choices available ashore with the next evolution of Paradise Collection by Carnival, the largest portfolio of exclusive destinations across The Bahamas, Caribbean and Mexico.

The collection includes six distinct destinations: Celebration Key in Grand Bahama; RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay; Isla Tropicale in Roatan; Amber Cove in the Dominican Republic; Puerta Maya in Cozumel and Grand Turk in Turks & Caicos.

Building on the early success of Celebration Key, which has welcomed more than 3.25 million guests since its opening in July 2025, Carnival revealed plans for two new expansion phases for the destination that will increase total land-side capacity by 6,000 guests, with 3,000 added in each phase.

In 2028, a new portal will introduce even more ways for guests to play and relax together with a heated, beach-entry pool with a swim-up bar; a new social waterslide designed for four to five guests to slide together; and a colorful, aqua play area featuring five waterslides, a dry climbing play structure and drenching bucket created especially for younger children.

In 2030, a new major water park will add 18 waterslides, the cruise industry's longest lazy river with float-up bars and swim-in/swim-out cabanas, as well as a new exclusive area with an infinity pool, more beach access and new dining and bar concepts.

Carnival also announced Serenity Beach, a new complimentary retreat for guests 21 and older coming to RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay in spring 2027. It will feature dedicated loungers and bar and beverage service, with daybeds and cabanas available for an additional charge.

Greater Value from Ship to Shore

Beginning in February 2027, Carnival will extend its drink packages CHEERS!, CHEERS! Zero Proof™, Bottomless Bubbles™ and CHEERS! Social to Celebration Key and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay, giving guests who purchase these Carnival packages greater value for their vacation dollars.

For additional information on Carnival Cruise Line and to book a cruise vacation on Carnival, call 1-800-CARNIVAL, visit http://carnival.com or contact your favorite travel advisor or online travel site.

ABOUT CARNIVAL CRUISE LINE

Carnival Cruise Line, part of Carnival Corporation (NYSE: CCL), the world's largest cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines operating in over 800 ports & destinations worldwide – and is proud to be known as America's Cruise Line and for carrying more Americans and serving more U.S. homeports than any other. Carnival sails more than six and a half million guests annually and in 2023 was the first cruise line to sail more than 100 million guests in total. Operating from 13 U.S. and four Australian homeports, as well as seasonally from Europe, Carnival hosts more than 95,000 guests on its ships every day of the year and employs more than 50,000 team members, representing 120 nationalities.

Since its founding in 1972, Carnival has continually revolutionized the cruise industry and popularized the cruise vacation as an affordable and fun travel option. Carnival's fleet of 29 ships reflects an exciting period of growth that continues with the addition of seven ships through 2035: a fourth and fifth Excel class ship scheduled for 2027 and 2028, respectively; three Ace class ships scheduled for delivery in 2029, 2031 and 2033, beginning with Carnival Destiny; and two additional ships in the new class expected to be delivered in 2033 and 2035. Carnival's newest guest offering is its all-new exclusive destination, Celebration Key on Grand Bahama, which debuted in 2025 to join the company's Paradise Collection of Caribbean gems.

TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Osisko Gold Group Inc. (NYSE: OGG, TSXV: OGG) ("Osisko Gold" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Wen Hou to the board of directors of the Company (the "Board"), effective immediately (the "Appointment"). Mr. Hou has been appointed to the Board as the nominee of Double Zero Capital, LP ("Double Zero"), the Company's largest shareholder with approximately 15.4% of the issued and outstanding common shares (on a non-diluted basis), pursuant to the investor rights agreement between the Company and Double Zero dated effective August 15, 2025 (the "Investor Rights Agreement").

"On behalf of the Board, we are pleased to welcome Wen as an independent director," commented Sean Roosen, Chairman and CEO. "Double Zero has been a strong supporter of the Company over the past year and a half, anchoring several key financings with cornerstone investments that were instrumental in advancing the Cariboo Gold Project toward a final investment decision and securing the required construction funding. Wen brings a unique capital markets perspective informed by more than a decade of investing experience across equities, commodities, futures, and digital technology coupled with a background in engineering. His appointment further aligns the Board with shareholders as we continue to execute on the construction of the Cariboo Gold Project toward first gold in 2029."

Mr. Hou is an investor and fund manager with more than a decade of experience investing across equities, commodities and futures. He is the founder and Chief Investment Officer of Coincident Capital, a hedge fund established in 2019 that focuses on discretionary trend-following strategies in commodities and digital asset markets. He also serves as a fund manager of Brand Name GP LLC, Double Zero's general partner. Mr. Hou leads the Hou Family Office, where he oversees its real estate investments and private equity arm, which invests in precious metals, commodity funds and trading, and early-stage artificial intelligence software companies. Prior to his investment career, Mr. Hou worked as an integrated circuit design engineer at Intel Corporation. Mr. Hou holds a Master of Science in Electrical Engineering from the Henry Samueli School of Engineering at the University of California, Irvine.

The Appointment remains subject to the final acceptance of the TSX Venture Exchange.

Osisko Gold Group Inc. is a continental North American gold development company focused on past producing mining camps with district-scale potential. OLD GREENWICH, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Ellington Credit Company (NYSE: EARN) ("we") today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

  • Net asset value (NAV) per share was $4.04 as of September 30, 2026, which includes the effects of distributions of $0.24 per share for the quarter.
  • GAAP net income was $3.7 million, or $0.09 per share.
  • Net investment income ("NII") was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.
    • Adjusted net investment income1 was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.
  • CLO portfolio was $332.0 million as of September 30, 2026.
    • CLO debt investments—$146.4 million
    • CLO equity investments—$185.6 million
    • Purchased $41.5 million of CLO investments and sold $31.5 million, across 61 trades.
  • Weighted average GAAP yield2 for the quarter, based on amortized cost, was 12.9% on the total CLO portfolio.
  • Received $14.5 million in recurring cash distributions3 from the CLO portfolio, or $0.37 per share.
  • Raised net proceeds of $5.5 million through the issuance of approximately 1.27 million common shares at prices representing a 3% weighted average premium to NAV per share.
  • Subsequent to quarter end, reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, effective with the distribution payable in January 2027.

Management Commentary

“Ellington Credit generated an economic return of 2.4% for the third calendar quarter, or 9.9% annualized, as our active trading and disciplined risk management helped us navigate renewed market volatility,” said Laurence Penn, Chief Executive Officer and President. “Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios both contributed positively, led by net investment income. Our credit hedges generated gains for the quarter and helped protect NAV per share as credit spreads widened in September. These positive contributions were partially offset by losses on interest rate hedges associated with our fixed-rate unsecured notes. We are proud to have continued our relative outperformance, generating positive GAAP earnings in a challenging quarter when the vast majority of our peers reported losses.

“We remained highly active during the quarter, executing 61 distinct CLO trades and continuing to rotate capital toward investments where we see more attractive risk-adjusted returns. Our overall portfolio size was roughly unchanged quarter over quarter, as sales, paydowns and deal calls largely offset new investment activity. Importantly, the weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, up from 14.9% in the second quarter.

“Adjusted net investment income increased by $0.02 sequentially to $0.17 per share, and we continue to see opportunities for further increases through additional capital deployment, selective use of leverage, and continued portfolio rotation. Our Board of Trustees has reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, or $0.15 per quarter, a level supported by our current NII. CLO Performance

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Morningstar LSTA U.S. Leveraged Loan Index generated a total return of 1.9%, despite persistent credit dispersion and renewed volatility toward quarter end. Returns were supported by investor demand for floating-rate assets, a recovery in certain discounted loans, particularly in the software sector, and refinancings and maturity extensions. Double-B- and single-B-rated loans generated positive returns over the quarter, while triple-C-rated loans underperformed as rising interest rates pressured highly leveraged borrowers, particularly in cable and telecommunications. Loan prices declined in late September amid heightened inflation concerns and broader market volatility.

The European leveraged loan market underperformed the U.S. market, with more pronounced weakness in lower-quality credits. Headwinds included uncertainty over France’s fiscal and political outlook, energy-price volatility, and some forced selling from European credit funds.

CLO performance was mixed, as constructive loan-market technicals were tempered by the late-quarter selloff. Within CLO mezzanine debt, shorter-spread-duration, more seasoned positions benefited from stronger performance in shorter-maturity loans and principal paydowns that reduced deal-level leverage and strengthened structural credit protections. Meanwhile, higher-quality CLO equity positions with longer reinvestment periods benefited from stronger-than-anticipated interest payments in July, while limited loan repricing activity continued to support excess spread and equity cash flows.

However, higher borrowing costs pressured highly leveraged borrowers, weighing on CLO investments — particularly European CLO equity and lower-rated debt positions — with greater exposure to lower-quality collateral. In September, CLO tranche spreads widened modestly, and CLO equity valuations came under renewed pressure as broader markets weakened.

Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios each generated positive results for the quarter, as net investment income more than offset net realized and unrealized losses in our CLO equity investments. Credit hedges generated gains for the quarter overall, including in September, helping cushion the impact of that month’s spread widening on NAV per share. Additional headwinds included losses on interest rate hedges associated with our unsecured notes, and mark-to-market losses on the notes themselves as credit spread tightening more than offset the impact of higher interest rates.

We executed 61 distinct CLO trades during the quarter, with sales and paydowns largely offsetting new investment activity. The weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, compared with 14.9% in the second quarter. At September 30, 2026, our CLO portfolio had a fair value of $332.0 million and a weighted average projected yield of 18.3% based on fair value.

Key Terms

collateralized loan obligationsfinancial
A collateralized loan obligation is a financial product that pools many corporate loans and repackages them into slices sold to investors, with some slices offering steady, lower returns and others offering higher returns but more risk. Like splitting a pizza into pieces for different tastes, CLOs let investors pick their preferred risk level and help banks fund lending, so changes in CLO performance influence credit availability and can move markets.
net asset valuefinancial
Net asset value is the total value of an investment fund's assets minus any liabilities, divided by the number of shares or units outstanding. It represents the per-share worth of the fund, similar to how the value of a house is determined by its total worth after debts are subtracted. Investors use it to gauge the true value of their holdings and to compare different investment options.
View in glossary
non-GAAP financial measurefinancial
A non-GAAP financial measure is a way companies present their financial results that excludes certain expenses or income to show how they believe their core business is performing. It matters because it can give a clearer picture of how the company is really doing, but it can also be used to make results look better than they actually are.
total return swapsfinancial
A total return swap is a contract where one party agrees to pay another the full economic performance—price changes plus income—of an asset, while the other party pays a regular fee or interest. Think of it like renting the gains and losses of a stock or bond without owning it: investors can gain exposure, hedge positions, or add leverage more cheaply, but they take on the risk that the counterparty might fail to honor payments and that synthetic holdings can affect leverage and transparency.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Endeavour Silver Corp. (“Endeavour” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce the results of a Feasibility Study (the “Study” or “FS”) for its Pitarrilla Project (“Pitarrilla” or the “Project”), located in Durango State, Mexico. All amounts are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise stated.

The Study evaluates the development of a mechanized, ramp-access underground mine focused on the Project’s sulphide mineralization and high-grade core. The proposed operation is designed at 4,000 tonnes per day (tpd) of processing capacity and would produce silver-lead and silver-zinc concentrates using conventional crushing, grinding and flotation, with filtered tailings planned for dry-stack facility.

The Study represents an important milestone in advancing Pitarrilla toward a development decision. The Company will file a technical report supporting the Study on SEDAR+ within 45 days of this news release, in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”).

Feasibility Study Highlights

  • Strong Project Economics: The project delivers an after-tax Net Present Value (NPV) of $736 million at a 5% discount rate and after-tax Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 16.37%, based on FS assumptions of $50.00 per ounce (oz) silver (Ag), $2,028.23/tonne (t) lead (Pb) and $2,733.70/t zinc (Zn)

  • Large-Scale, Long-Life Production: Planned average annual production of approximately 5.4 Moz of silver, 13 kt of lead, 29 kt of zinc and 7.5 Moz silver equivalent(1) (AgEq) over an 18-year mine life (LOM), highlighted by average annual production of 7.9 Moz AgEq for the first 5 years of full operation

  • Key Permits Supporting Development: Key permits are in place for water use and discharge, explosives, change of land use, development and underground mining. Additional approvals and amendments remain outstanding, including the Tailings Storage Facility Permit (TSF)

  • Resilience at Lower Silver Prices: Pitarrilla has an estimated break-even silver price below $30 per ounce, compared with the base-case silver price of $50 per ounce, providing a margin against lower silver prices while maintaining leverage to higher silver prices

  • Capital Investment for Long-Term Growth: Planned initial capital(2) of approximately $585 million, including $65 million of contingency, with sustaining capital(2) of approximately $119 million over the life of mine. Approximately 16.7 kilometres of development over the LOM provides access to over 25 million ore tonnes

  • Low-Cost Production Supporting Cash Flow Potential: Planned LOM average cash costs(2), net of by-product credits, of $12.66 per payable silver oz and mine-site all-in sustaining costs(2) (AISC) of $15.06 per payable silver oz support a low-cost operating profile

  • Well Positioned to Fund Construction: Endeavour expects to fund the majority of construction of Pitarrilla through a combination of cash on hand and cash flow from its operating mines, providing flexibility as the Project advances toward a development decision

  • Mechanized Underground Mining: A ramp-access underground mine is designed to support planned production averaging approximately 4,000 tpd, utilizing long-hole stoping and development in ore

  • Conventional Processing: The processing flowsheet includes crushing, grinding and flotation, followed by concentrate thickening and filtration. Filtered tailings are planned for storage in a dry-stack facility

  • Established Infrastructure and Access: The Project benefits from year-round road access, connections to power and water infrastructure and existing exploration and contractor camps

  • Significant Opportunities to Enhance Value: Resource conversion, exploration upside, open-pit optionality and further mine-plan, processing and cost optimization offer additional potential to enhance long-term value

“We are excited by the strong Feasibility Study results, which mark a major milestone for Pitarrilla and highlight a compelling opportunity for Endeavour’s next phase of organic growth,” commented Dan Dickson, Chief Executive Officer. “With an anticipated initial 18-year mine life, substantial silver production and an extremely attractive operating cost profile, Pitarrilla has the potential to become a cornerstone asset that delivers lasting value for our shareholders.”

Location and Access

Pitarrilla is located within the Municipalities of El Oro and Inde, on the eastern flank of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range in the central part of Durango State, Mexico. The city of Durango, the capital of Durango state, is located 160 kilometres south of the property and the major city of Torreón 160 kilometres to the east.

Pitarrilla is accessible by regional roads. Planned primary access follows approximately 47 kilometres of existing roads, with secondary access via El Palmito. Required upgrades include a permanent bridge over the Nazas River, approximately 11 kilometres from the property.


Property, History, Geology, Mineralization

Pitarrilla is formed by 5 contiguous mineral concessions entitled to Minera Pitarrilla S.A. de C.V. (“Minera Pitarrilla”) and covering a total area of approximately 4,950 hectares. Minera Pitarrilla is a Mexican corporate entity, and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Endeavour. 

The Sierra Madre mountain range preserves remnants of one of Earth’s largest accumulations of intermediate to felsic volcanic rocks, formed in a calc-alkaline magmatic arc during the Eocene to early Miocene, approximately 52–25 million years ago. This volcanism intermittently generated numerous medium- to high-level hydrothermal systems enriched to varying degrees in Ag, Au, Pb and Zn, including epithermal systems in the major Mexican silver districts of the states of Guanajuato, Zacatecas, Durango and Chihuahua. Pitarrilla’s silver-lead-zinc mineralization lies within the Central Mexican Silver Belt, a metallogenic province encompassing these districts. 

Endeavour purchased Pitarrilla from SSR Mining Inc. (SSR) for $70 million in 2022, consisting of $35 million in common shares and a further $35 million in cash or in common shares at the election of SSR and agreed to by the Company, and a grant of a 1.25% NSR royalty.

Mine Plan and Production Profile

Pitarrilla is planned as a mechanized, ramp-access underground mine capable of supplying approximately 4,000 tonnes per day to the processing plant. The current design contemplates a mining mix weighted toward transverse and longitudinal long-hole stoping, supplemented by development in ore. The mine plan is expected to target the sulphide mineralization, including Manto Pitarrilla and associated feeder structures. The readily accessible Manto Pitarrilla deposit configuration supports an efficient mine layout with relatively limited underground development required over the LOM. Approximately 16.7 kilometres of total development is planned, comprising 5.4 kilometres during the initial years and 11.3 kilometres of sustaining development thereafter, providing access to the deposit while supporting operating flexibility and efficient, low-cost mining. The current mine plan includes stockpiling over 600,000 tonnes of ore during the construction phase.  

Processing and Infrastructure

The proposed 4,000 tpd process plant is expected to include crushing, a grinding circuit incorporating a primary ball mill and a semi-autogenous grinding (SAG) mill, flash, rougher, scavenger and cleaner flotation, concentrate thickening and filtration, and a tailings filtration plant. Filtered tailings are planned to be placed in a dry-stack storage facility. Pitarrilla benefits from year-round road access and an established project footprint with power and water access, exploration infrastructure, contractor facilities and regional access to an experienced workforce.

Capital Investment, Operating Costs and Cash Flow

Initial capital(2) to develop Pitarrilla is estimated at $585 million and is expected to be incurred over a 30-month construction period. Cumulative sustaining capital(2) is estimated at $119 million. Sustaining expenditures are expected to be front-end loaded, as the readily accessible Manto Pitarrilla deposit requires relatively limited development later in the mine life, supporting lower ongoing capital requirements and significant operating flexibility.

LOM average direct production costs(2) are estimated at $109.24 per tonne processed, with cash costs(2), net of by-product credits, of $12.66 per payable oz silver and mine-site AISC(2) (including royalties and special mining duties), net of by-product credits, of $15.06 per payable oz silver.

During full years of commercial production, average annual after-tax free cash flow(1) is estimated at approximately $136 million.

Opportunities to Unlock Further Value

  • Resource Conversion and Mine-Life Extension: Convert additional Inferred Mineral Resources to higher-confidence categories through targeted drilling and evaluate opportunities to incorporate suitable material into future mine plans. The current mine plan is based on a 150 g/t cut-off grade. A sustained higher metal price environment could support a lower cut-off grade, potentially extending mine life significantly by incorporating additional mineralized material with grades modestly below those included in the current mine plan
  • Metallurgical Evaluation: The feasibility study mine plan excludes 18.4 million tonnes of mineral resources within the transition zone. This represents a significant opportunity to further evaluate the metallurgical characteristics of this material and potentially incorporate these resources into future mine plans, leveraging existing infrastructure with minimal additional mine development requirements
  • Exploration Upside: Test extensions of the Pitarrilla mineralization, in feeder structures which remains open at depth, and other priority targets across the property that could add higher-grade tonnes or extend the production profile
  • Future Open-Pit Potential: The underground sulphide strategy preserves the broader resource base, maintaining the potential to evaluate future open-pit development of Indicated and Inferred Mineral Resources, providing an additional pathway for long-term growth and value creation

Non-IFRS Financial Measures

The Company has included certain non-IFRS measures in this document as discussed below.  The Company believes that these measures, in addition to conventional measures prepared in accordance with IFRS, provide investors an improved ability to evaluate the underlying performance of the Company.  The non-IFRS measures are intended to provide additional information and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures of performance prepared in accordance with IFRS.  These measures do not have any standardized meaning prescribed under IFRS, and therefore may not be comparable to other issuers.

Please see the September 30, 2026 MD&A for explanations and discussion of these non-IFRS and other non-financial measures and ratios. Certain additional disclosures for these non-IFRS measures have been incorporated by reference and can be found in the section “Non-IFRS Measures” in the September 30, 2026 MD&A available on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.com.

Cash cost (“Cash cost”) per ounce

Cash cost per ounce is a non-IFRS measure.  In the silver mining industry, this metric is a common performance measure that does not have a standardized meaning under IFRS.  Cash costs include direct costs (including smelting, refining, transportation and selling costs), royalties and special mining duty and changes in finished goods inventory net of by-product credits. 

Mine Site - All-in sustaining costs (“MAISC”) and All-in sustaining cost (“AISC”) per ounce

MAISC and AISC per ounce are non- IFRS measures.  These measures are intended to assist readers in evaluating the total cost of producing silver from operations.  While there is no standardized meaning across the industry for AISC measures, the Company’s definition conforms to the definition of AISC as set out by the World Gold Council and used as a standard of the Silver Institute.  The Company defines AISC as the cash operating costs (as defined above), reclamation cost accretion, mine site expensed exploration, corporate general and administration costs and sustaining capital expenditures. For the purpose of this press release, MAISC does not include corporate general and administration costs or mine site expensed exploration.

Free cash flow

In the mining industry, free cash flow is a common performance measure with no standardized meaning.  The Company calculates free cash flow by deducting cash capital spending (capital expenditures, net of expenditures paid through finance leases) from net cash provided by operating activities.

The Company discloses free cash flow as it believes the measure provides valuable assistance to investors and analysts in evaluating the Company’s ability to generate cash flow after capital investments and build the cash resources of the Company.

Initial and sustaining capital

Initial and sustaining capital are non-IFRS measures.  Initial capital is defined as capital required to develop and construct to bring the mine to commercial production and sustaining capital is defined as the capital required to maintain operations at existing levels.  Both measurements are used by management to assess the effectiveness of an investment program.

Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (“EBITDA”)

EBITDA represents net earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.  EBITDA is an indicator of the Company’s ability to generate liquidity by producing operating cash flow to fund working capital needs, service debt obligations, and fund capital expenditures.

Gross revenue and Gross Cost of Sales

Gross revenue represents gross sales of metals and is calculated by adjusting net revenue for the removal of treatment, refining and transportation costs.  Gross cost of sales is calculated by adjusting cost of sales for the inclusion of treatment, refining and transportation costs.
